column1: # Arms whose failure cannot say what it measured (#1164). suite<TAB>check name.
# A DEBT, and the gate refuses BOTH directions: a new offender not listed here
# fails BY NAME, and a listed arm that has since been repaired fails until its
# row is removed -- so the list may only shrink, by construction, and nobody has
# to police a number. The count is DERIVED from the rows rather than typed, so
# the two cannot disagree the way a hand-maintained total does.
# WITH ONE EXCEPTION, AND IT IS NOT AN ESCAPE HATCH: WIDENING THE SWEEP ADDS
# ROWS. The list is the debt of the shapes the sweep can SEE, so teaching it a
# new shape uncovers arms that were always broken and never looked at. It went
# 77 -> 103 under #1174, when awk-rendered verdicts came into scope; not one of
# those 26 arms changed, only what was examined. A growth of this list is
# therefore a claim that the SWEEP changed, and a reviewer should refuse any
# addition that does not come with one.
# AND THAT CLAIM IS CHECKABLE RATHER THAN TRUSTED. "Not one of those 26 arms
# changed" is readable straight off the diff, because the widening touches this
# list and the sweep and nothing else:
# THREE DOTS, against the merge base. Two dots compares the working tree with
# whatever main has moved on to, so a branch that is merely BEHIND main lists
# every file the other lane touched -- four of them, in the run that caught this
# wording. A suite appearing in the three-dot list beside a growth of this file
# is the shape to refuse: the rows would then be describing arms the same commit
# edited, and "only what was examined changed" would no longer be true.
# KEYED BY (SUITE, NAME), never by name alone: `premise: the install script
# declares MODULE_PATHNAME symbols at all` is carried by two suites, and one key
# for both would let a repair in one be satisfied by the other. Never by
# file:line either -- a line number moves under any edit above it and a rebase
# GENERATED BY THE SWEEP THAT CHECKS IT, in
# file are what validate the sweep; this list is only its output. An earlier
# draft generated the list with a second implementation, and the two disagreed
# in BOTH directions: the generator required `|| echo` and missed ten
# `&& echo ok` arms, which are worse (`got [] want [ok]` loses the measurement
# AND the verdict); the sweep searched for a unary operator anywhere in the test
# and read `grep -c .` as a file test, excusing five real offenders. Both bugs
# were found by the disagreement and neither by either half alone.
# AND CONTINUATIONS ARE FOLDED BEFORE SWEEPING. A line-by-line reader sees
# $ROWS_BEFORE)"` on the next line, so four arms that DO carry their values read
# as though they discard them. 65 rows before folding, 61 after, and the four
# removed were named rather than counted. Found because the reviewer asked
# whether any no-else arm had an empty WANT -- it did not, and looking answered a
# 61 -> 60 when #1165 repaired `native_fetch_coalesce: a wide index fetch does
# not pin once per column`. The row was removed because the sweep stopped finding
# it, not because anyone edited this file: that is the "repaired arm" direction
# doing its job, and it is why the list is regenerated rather than hand-edited.#
# 60 -> 77 when the scope was narrowed from the DIRECTORY test/selftest/ to the
# single file that enforces the rule. The first draft excluded the whole
# directory on a justification that is true of 540 and of no other part; 17 real
# offenders were sitting in parts the sweep never looked at, including
# 410's two computed line numbers compared with `-lt` and both discarded.
# Reported by @OffgridwithJD, who planted five shapes against the controls and
# found this one by asking what the sweep was never SHOWN rather than what it
# got wrong on what it was.
# 70 -> 136 WHEN TESTS CHAINED OUTSIDE THE BRACKETS CAME INTO SCOPE (#1997).
# `[ A ] && [ B ] && echo yes || echo no` is a compound: `no` does not say
# which test failed. The sweep read only the first test, so these arms were
# never examined. The 66 new rows are that claim, and it is checkable off the
# diff: no arm they name is touched by the change that added them. Selftest
# 250 has 10 of the rows and the same change edits it, but only to repair a
# different arm, `premise: stripping comments leaves the runner's code behind`
# (#2002). The sweep now also joins a line that ends in `&&` or `||` to the

# THE SAME CHANGE REPAIRED SEVEN ARMS AND ADDED NO ROW FOR THEM (#2002). A `]`
